Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 52, verse 1–16 (part 1 of 2):

Tafsir of Surat al-Tur (The Mount)
It is Meccan.

Malik narrated from al-Zuhri, from Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im, from his father: "I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) reciting al-Tur in the Maghrib prayer, and I did not hear anyone with a more beautiful voice or recitation than his."

Al-Bukhari and Muslim both reported it through the chain of Malik. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4845), and Sahih Muslim, no. (463).] Al-Bukhari also said:

Abdullah ibn Yusuf narrated to us: Malik informed us, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Nawfal, from Urwa, from Zaynab bint Abi Salama, from Umm Salama, who said: "I complained to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that I was unwell, and he said: 'Circumambulate behind the people while you are riding.' So I circumambulated, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was praying beside the House, reciting al-Tur and 'a Book inscribed'." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4853), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1276).]

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

* *

Allah, the Exalted, swears by His creations, which indicate His great power, that His punishment is certain to befall His enemies and that none can repel it from them. Al-Tur is the mountain that has trees on it, like the one upon which Allah spoke to Musa and from which Isa was sent. A mountain without trees is not called tur; it is simply called jabal (mountain).

﴿And a Book inscribed﴾. It was said: this is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz). And it was said: it refers to the revealed books, written down and read out to the people openly. For this reason He said: ﴿in parchment unrolled, and the frequented House﴾. It is established in the two Sahihs that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said in the hadith of the Isra' (Night Journey), after passing to the seventh heaven: "Then I was raised to the frequented House, and behold, seventy thousand [angels] enter it every day, and they do not return to it until the last of them [returns]." That is, they worship and circumambulate in it, just as the people of the earth circumambulate their Ka'ba. That House is the Ka'ba of the people of the seventh heaven. For this reason Ibrahim the Friend (al-Khalil), peace be upon him, was found leaning his back against the frequented House, because he was the builder of the earthly Ka'ba. The recompense is of the same kind as the deed. It is directly opposite the Ka'ba. In every heaven there is a House in which its inhabitants worship and toward which they pray. The one in the lowest heaven is called Bayt al-'Izza. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Hisham ibn Ammar narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, Rawh ibn Janah narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "In the seventh heaven there is a House called 'al-Ma'mur', directly opposite the Ka'ba. In the fourth heaven there is a river called 'al-Hayawan' which Jibril enters every day, plunging into it once; then he emerges and shakes himself so that seventy thousand drops fall from him. Allah creates from each drop an angel who are commanded to come to the House al-Ma'mur and pray in it. They do so, then they leave and never return to it again, and one of them is appointed over them, commanded to stand with them at a station in the heaven where they glorify Allah until the Hour is established."

This is a very strange (gharib) hadith; Rawh ibn Janah alone transmitted it. He is al-Qurashi al-Umawi, their client, Abu Sa'd al-Dimashqi. A group of hadith memorizers criticized this hadith from him, among them al-Jawzajani, al-Uqayli, al-Hakim Abu Abd Allah al-Naysaburi, and others.

Al-Hakim said: "It has no basis from the hadith of Abu Hurayra, nor Sa'id, nor al-Zuhri." [Ibn Adi narrated it in al-Kamil (3/144) through the chain of Hisham ibn Ammar, and said: "I heard Ibn Hammad say: al-Sa'di said: Rawh ibn Janah reported from al-Zuhri a mu'dal hadith about the frequented House," then he related it with its chain and followed it with: "This hadith is known only through Rawh ibn Janah from al-Zuhri."]

Ibn Jarir said: Hannad ibn al-Sarri narrated to us, Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Khalid ibn Urar'ara, that a man asked Ali: "What is the frequented House?" He said: "It is a House in the heaven called 'al-Darah' (al-Dud̤rāḥ), directly above the Ka'ba; its sanctity in the heaven is like the sanctity of the House on earth. Seventy thousand angels pray in it every day, and then they do not return to it ever." [Tafsir al-Tabari (27/10).]

Similarly it was narrated by Shu'ba and Sufyan al-Thawri, from Simak, and in their version the one who asked was Ibn al-Kawwa. Then Ibn Jarir narrated it from Abu Kurayb, from Talq ibn Ghannam, from Za'ida, from Asim, from Ali ibn Rabi'a, who said: "Ibn al-Kawwa asked Ali about the frequented House. He said: 'It is a mosque in the heaven called al-Darah; seventy thousand angels enter it every day, then they never return to it.'" He also narrated it from the hadith of Abu al-Tufayl, from Ali, with the same wording.

Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas: "It is a House opposite the Throne, which the angels frequent; seventy thousand angels pray in it every day, then they do not return to it." Ikrima, Mujahid, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, al-Suddi, and many of the early scholars said likewise.

Qatada said: "It was mentioned to us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said one day to his companions: 'Do you know what the frequented House is?' They said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'It is a mosque in the heaven, directly opposite the Ka'ba; were it to fall, it would fall upon it. Seventy thousand angels pray in it every day, and when they leave, they do not return, the last of them.'"

Al-Dahhak claimed that a group of angels called al-Hin, from the tribe of Iblis, populate it. [Tafsir al-Tabari (27/11).] And Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿and the raised ceiling﴾. Sufyan al-Thawri, Shu'ba, and Abu al-Ahwas narrated from Simak, from Khalid ibn Arar'ara, from Ali: "﴿and the raised ceiling﴾ means the sky." Sufyan said: Then he recited ﴿And We made the sky a protected ceiling, yet they turn away from its signs﴾ [al-Anbiya': 32]. Likewise said Mujahid, Qatada, al-Suddi, Ibn Jurayj, and Ibn Zayd, and Ibn Jarir chose this view.

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: it is the Throne, meaning that it is a ceiling for all created things, and it has a direction, and it is intended together with other things, as the majority said.

* *

His saying: ﴿and the sea filled with fire (al-masjur)﴾. Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: it is the water beneath the Throne, from which Allah sends down the rain by which He gives life to bodies in their graves on the day of their return. The majority said: it is this sea. There is disagreement about the meaning of His saying ﴿al-masjur﴾. Some said: the meaning is that it will be kindled with fire on the Day of Resurrection, like His saying: ﴿and when the seas are set ablaze﴾ [al-Takwir: 6], that is, set on fire, so that it becomes a blazing fire surrounding the people of the place of standing. This was narrated by Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab from Ali ibn Abi Talib, and it was also reported from Ibn Abbas. Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Abd Allah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr, and others also said this.

Al-Ala' ibn Badr said: it is called the masjur sea only because no water is drunk from it and no crops are watered by it, and likewise the seas on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated this from him.

From Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿and the sea al-masjur﴾ means "the released (al-mursal)." Qatada said: ﴿and the sea al-masjur﴾ means "the full (al-mamlu')." Ibn Jarir chose this and argued that it is not kindled today, so it is full.

It was also said: the meaning is "the empty." Al-Asma'i said, from Abu Amr ibn al-Ala', from Dhu al-Rumma, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿and the sea al-masjur﴾: "It means the empty. A community went out seeking water, then returned and said: 'The pool is masjur,' meaning empty." Ibn Mardawayh narrated it in the Musnad of the poets.

It was also said: al-masjur means "restrained, held back from the earth, so that it does not flood it and drown its people." This was said by Ali ibn Abi Talha from Ibn Abbas, and al-Suddi and others said likewise. The hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, in his Musnad, indicates this, for he said:

Yazid narrated to us, al-Awwam narrated to us, a shaykh who was stationed on the coast narrated to me, saying: I met Abu Salih, the client of Umar ibn al-Khattab, and he said: Umar ibn al-Khattab narrated to us, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "There is no night but that the sea rises over them three times, asking Allah to burst upon them, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, restrains it." [Al-Musnad (1/43). It was also narrated by Ibn al-Jawzi in al-'Ilal al-Mutanahiya (1/52), who said: "al-Awwam is weak, and the shaykh is unknown."]

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Isma'ili said: Al-Hasan ibn Sufyan narrated to us, from Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, from Yazid, that is Ibn Harun, from al-Awwam ibn Hawshab, who said: a stationed shaykh narrated to me: "I went out one night for my watch, and no one else from the guard had gone out except me. I came to the harbour and climbed up, and it kept appearing to me that the sea was rising to the level of the mountain peaks. This happened several times while I was awake. Then I met Abu Salih, and he said: Umar ibn al-Khattab narrated to us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'There is no night but that the sea rises three times, asking Allah to burst upon them, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, restrains it.'" In its chain is an unnamed man. [The author mentioned it in the Musnad of Umar (2/608) from the narration of al-Isma'ili, and said: "In it is an unnamed man who was not named, and Allah knows best his condition."]

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is surely going to occur﴾. This is what is sworn to: that it is going to fall upon the disbelievers, as He said in another verse: ﴿there is none to repel it﴾, meaning there is no repeller to ward it off from them when Allah wills it for them.

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Dunya said: My father narrated to us, Musa ibn Dawud narrated to us, from Salih al-Muri, from Ja'far ibn Zayd al-Abdi, who said: Umar went out patrolling Medina one night, and passed by the house of a Muslim man, and found him standing in prayer. He stopped to listen to his recitation, and he recited: ﴿By the Tur﴾ until he reached ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is surely going to occur; there is none to repel it﴾. Umar said: "An oath, by the Lord of the Ka'ba, is true." So he dismounted from his donkey and leaned against a wall, and he remained there for a long time. Then he returned to his home, and he stayed sick for a month, while people visited him without knowing what his illness was. May Allah be pleased with him. [The author mentioned it in the Musnad of Umar (2/608) from the narration of Ibn Abi al-Dunya, and its chain includes Salih al-Muri; in the Musnad of Umar it is written "al-Madani," and if it is al-Muri, he is weak.]

Abu Ubayd said in Fada'il al-Quran: Muhammad ibn Salih narrated to us, Hisham ibn Hassan narrated to us, from al-Hasan: that Umar recited ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is surely going to occur; there is none to repel it﴾, and he cried out with a great sob, and he was ill for twenty days because of it. [Fada'il al-Quran of Abu Ubayd (p. 64).]

* *

His saying: ﴿on the Day when the sky will sway violently﴾. Ibn Abbas and Qatada said: it will move with a great movement. From Ibn Abbas: it is its splitting. Mujahid said: it will revolve in a revolution. Al-Dahhak said: its turning around and its moving at Allah's command, and parts of it surging over other parts. This is the view chosen by Ibn Jarir, that it is movement in a circular motion. He said: Abu Ubayda Ma'mar ibn al-Muthanna recited the verse of al-A'sha:

"As if her walk, from the house of her neighbour, / is the sway of a cloud, neither slow nor hasty."

﴿and the mountains will move, moving﴾, that is, they will go away and become scattered dust, and be blown away as dust.

﴿So woe that Day to those who deny﴾: that is, woe to them on that Day, from the punishment of God, His retribution against them, and His chastisement of them.

﴿who are playing in plunging about﴾: that is, in the world they plunge into falsehood and take their religion as mockery and play.

﴿The Day they are pushed toward the fire of Hell with a violent push﴾: that is, they are shoved and driven. Mujahid, al-Sha'bi, Muhammad ibn Ka'b, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi and al-Thawri said: they are pushed into it with force.

﴿This is the Fire which you used to deny﴾: that is, the guardians of Hell (al-Zabaniyah) will say this to them as rebuke and reproach.

﴿Is this magic, or do you not see? Burn in it﴾: that is, enter it, entering as one who is overwhelmed by it from all directions. ﴿So be patient or be not patient; it is all the same for you﴾: that is, whether you endure its punishment and torment or do not endure, there is no escape for you from it and no deliverance from it [[In manuscript A: "fīhā" (in it).]]. ﴿You are only being recompensed for what you used to do﴾: that is, God does not wrong anyone, but repays each person for his deeds.

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: it is the water beneath the Throne, from which Allah sends down the rain by which He gives life to bodies in their graves on the day of their return. The majority said: it is this sea. There is disagreement about the meaning of His saying ﴿al-masjur﴾. Some said: the meaning is that it will be kindled with fire on the Day of Resurrection, like His saying: ﴿and when the seas are set ablaze﴾ [al-Takwir: 6], that is, set on fire, so that it becomes a blazing fire surrounding the people of the place of standing. This was narrated by Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab from Ali ibn Abi Talib, and it was also reported from Ibn Abbas. Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Abd Allah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr, and others also said this.

Al-Ala' ibn Badr said: it is called the masjur sea only because no water is drunk from it and no crops are watered by it, and likewise the seas on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated this from him.

From Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿and the sea al-masjur﴾ means "the released (al-mursal)." Qatada said: ﴿and the sea al-masjur﴾ means "the full (al-mamlu')." Ibn Jarir chose this and argued that it is not kindled today, so it is full.

It was also said: the meaning is "the empty." Al-Asma'i said, from Abu Amr ibn al-Ala', from Dhu al-Rumma, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿and the sea al-masjur﴾: "It means the empty. A community went out seeking water, then returned and said: 'The pool is masjur,' meaning empty." Ibn Mardawayh narrated it in the Musnad of the poets.

It was also said: al-masjur means "restrained, held back from the earth, so that it does not flood it and drown its people." This was said by Ali ibn Abi Talha from Ibn Abbas, and al-Suddi and others said likewise. The hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, in his Musnad, indicates this, for he said:

Yazid narrated to us, al-Awwam narrated to us, a shaykh who was stationed on the coast narrated to me, saying: I met Abu Salih, the client of Umar ibn al-Khattab, and he said: Umar ibn al-Khattab narrated to us, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "There is no night but that the sea rises over them three times, asking Allah to burst upon them, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, restrains it." [Al-Musnad (1/43). It was also narrated by Ibn al-Jawzi in al-'Ilal al-Mutanahiya (1/52), who said: "al-Awwam is weak, and the shaykh is unknown."]

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Isma'ili said: Al-Hasan ibn Sufyan narrated to us, from Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, from Yazid, that is Ibn Harun, from al-Awwam ibn Hawshab, who said: a stationed shaykh narrated to me: "I went out one night for my watch, and no one else from the guard had gone out except me. I came to the harbour and climbed up, and it kept appearing to me that the sea was rising to the level of the mountain peaks. This happened several times while I was awake. Then I met Abu Salih, and he said: Umar ibn al-Khattab narrated to us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'There is no night but that the sea rises three times, asking Allah to burst upon them, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, restrains it.'" In its chain is an unnamed man. [The author mentioned it in the Musnad of Umar (2/608) from the narration of al-Isma'ili, and said: "In it is an unnamed man who was not named, and Allah knows best his condition."]

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is surely going to occur﴾. This is what is sworn to: that it is going to fall upon the disbelievers, as He said in another verse: ﴿there is none to repel it﴾, meaning there is no repeller to ward it off from them when Allah wills it for them.

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Dunya said: My father narrated to us, Musa ibn Dawud narrated to us, from Salih al-Muri, from Ja'far ibn Zayd al-Abdi, who said: Umar went out patrolling Medina one night, and passed by the house of a Muslim man, and found him standing in prayer. He stopped to listen to his recitation, and he recited: ﴿By the Tur﴾ until he reached ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is surely going to occur; there is none to repel it﴾. Umar said: "An oath, by the Lord of the Ka'ba, is true." So he dismounted from his donkey and leaned against a wall, and he remained there for a long time. Then he returned to his home, and he stayed sick for a month, while people visited him without knowing what his illness was. May Allah be pleased with him. [The author mentioned it in the Musnad of Umar (2/608) from the narration of Ibn Abi al-Dunya, and its chain includes Salih al-Muri; in the Musnad of Umar it is written "al-Madani," and if it is al-Muri, he is weak.]

Abu Ubayd said in Fada'il al-Quran: Muhammad ibn Salih narrated to us, Hisham ibn Hassan narrated to us, from al-Hasan: that Umar recited ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is surely going to occur; there is none to repel it﴾, and he cried out with a great sob, and he was ill for twenty days because of it. [Fada'il al-Quran of Abu Ubayd (p. 64).]

* *

His saying: ﴿on the Day when the sky will sway violently﴾. Ibn Abbas and Qatada said: it will move with a great movement. From Ibn Abbas: it is its splitting. Mujahid said: it will revolve in a revolution. Al-Dahhak said: its turning around and its moving at Allah's command, and parts of it surging over other parts. This is the view chosen by Ibn Jarir, that it is movement in a circular motion. He said: Abu Ubayda Ma'mar ibn al-Muthanna recited the verse of al-A'sha:

"As if her walk, from the house of her neighbour, / is the sway of a cloud, neither slow nor hasty."

﴿and the mountains will move, moving﴾, that is, they will go away and become scattered dust, and be blown away as dust.

﴿So woe that Day to those who deny﴾: that is, woe to them on that Day, from the punishment of God, His retribution against them, and His chastisement of them.

﴿who are playing in plunging about﴾: that is, in the world they plunge into falsehood and take their religion as mockery and play.

﴿The Day they are pushed toward the fire of Hell with a violent push﴾: that is, they are shoved and driven. Mujahid, al-Sha'bi, Muhammad ibn Ka'b, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi and al-Thawri said: they are pushed into it with force.

﴿This is the Fire which you used to deny﴾: that is, the guardians of Hell (al-Zabaniyah) will say this to them as rebuke and reproach.

﴿Is this magic, or do you not see? Burn in it﴾: that is, enter it, entering as one who is overwhelmed by it from all directions. ﴿So be patient or be not patient; it is all the same for you﴾: that is, whether you endure its punishment and torment or do not endure, there is no escape for you from it and no deliverance from it [[In manuscript A: "fīhā" (in it).]]. ﴿You are only being recompensed for what you used to do﴾: that is, God does not wrong anyone, but repays each person for his deeds.

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 52, verses 17–20:

Allah, exalted is He, informs us about the state of the blessed, saying: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and bliss﴾, which is the opposite of what those (the disbelievers) are in of punishment and torment.

﴿Enjoying what their Lord has given them﴾, meaning they delight in what Allah has given them of blessings, of all kinds of pleasures: foods, drinks, clothing, dwellings, mounts, and other things. ﴿And their Lord has protected them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire﴾, meaning He has saved them from the punishment of the Fire. This is a blessing in its own right, separate from what is added to it, which is entry into Paradise, where there is joy such as no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Eat and drink with satisfaction for what you used to do﴾, it is like His saying: ﴿Eat and drink with satisfaction for what you put forward in the days gone by﴾ [al-Haqqah: 24]. That is, this is in return for that, as a favour and a kindness from Him.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Reclining on couches arranged in rows﴾, al-Thawri reported from Husayn, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas: "The couches are in canopies (hijal)."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, Safwan ibn Amr narrated to us, that he heard al-Haytham ibn Malik al-Ta'i say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A man will recline on a couch for forty years without turning from it or growing weary of it, and whatever his soul desires and his eye delights in will be brought to him."

And my father narrated to us, Hudba ibn Khalid narrated to us, from Sulayman ibn al-Mughira, from Thabit, who said: It has reached us that a man will recline in Paradise for seventy years, with his wives, his servants, and what Allah has given him of honour and bliss. Then when he glances, he sees wives he had never seen before, and they say: "The time has come for you to give us a share of you."

The meaning of ﴿arranged in rows﴾ is that the faces of some of them are turned toward others, as in His saying: ﴿on couches facing one another﴾ [as-Saffat: 44]. ﴿And We will marry them to fair, large-eyed women﴾, meaning We will make them companions, virtuous and beautiful wives, from among the large-eyed maidens (hur 'in).

Mujahid said: ﴿And We will marry them﴾ means We will wed them to large-eyed maidens. Their description has already been given in more than one place, so there is no need to repeat it.

He, may He be exalted, informs of His grace, generosity, kindness, gentleness toward His creation, and beneficence: that when the believers are followed by their offspring in faith, He joins them to their fathers in rank, even if their offspring do not reach their deeds, so that the fathers' eyes may be gladdened by their children being with them in their dwellings. Thus He brings them together in the best manner, by raising the one who is deficient in deeds to the level of the one who has complete deeds, without diminishing anything from the latter's deeds or rank, for the equality between him and that other. For this reason He said: ﴿And We join with them their offspring, and We deprive them not of anything of their deeds.﴾

Al-Thawri related from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Indeed Allah raises the offspring of the believer to his rank, even if they are below him in deeds, so that his eye may be gladdened by them." Then he recited: ﴿And those who believed and whose offspring followed them in faith, We join with them their offspring, and We deprive them not of anything of their deeds.﴾

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related it from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri, with the same chain. Likewise Ibn Jarir related it from the hadith of Shu'bah, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, with the same chain [[Tafsir al-Tabari (27/15).]]. Al-Bazzar related it from Sahl ibn Bahr [[In A: "Yahya".]], from al-Hasan ibn Hammad al-Warraq, from Qays ibn al-Rabi', from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Sa'id, from Ibn 'Abbas, as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet) report, and then mentioned it. He said: "Al-Thawri also related it from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Sa'id, from Ibn 'Abbas, as a mawquf (ending with Ibn 'Abbas) report" [[Musnad al-Bazzar no. (2260), Kashf al-Astar. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/114): "In it is Qays ibn al-Rabi', whom Shu'bah and al-Thawri declared trustworthy, but there is weakness in him."]].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-'Abbas ibn al-Walid ibn Mazid [[In M and A: "Yazid".]] al-Bayruti narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb [[In M: "Shu'bah".]] informed me, Shayban informed me, Layth informed me, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit al-Asadi, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And those who believed and whose offspring followed them in faith, We join with them their offspring﴾. He said: "They are the offspring of the believer who die upon faith. If the ranks of their fathers are higher than their ranks, they are joined to their fathers, and they are not diminished in the deeds they performed at all."

Al-Hafiz al-Tabarani said: al-Husayn ibn Ishaq al-Tustari narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghazwan narrated to us, Shurayk narrated to us, from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, - I think he traced it to the Prophet ﷺ - who said: "When a man enters Paradise, he asks about his parents, his wife, and his children. It is said: 'They did not reach your rank.' He says: 'O Lord, I did deeds for myself and for them.' So it is commanded that they be joined to him." And Ibn 'Abbas recited: ﴿And those who believed and whose offspring followed them in faith﴾, the verse [[Related by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (11/440): "Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Hadrami narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghazwan narrated to us" with it. And in al-Mu'jam al-Saghir no. (640): "'Abd Allah ibn Yazid al-Daqiqi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghazwan narrated to us" with it. And I did not find the narration of al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim al-Tustari.]].

Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning this verse: He says: "Those whose offspring were reached by faith and who acted in obedience to Me - I join them, by their faith, to Paradise, and their young children are joined to them."

This returns to the first explanation, for that one is explained more clearly than this. Likewise say al-Sha'bi, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ibrahim, Qatadah, Abu Salih, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, al-Dahhak, and Ibn Zayd. It is also the choice of Ibn Jarir. 'Abd Allah ibn al-Imam Ahmad said:

'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Hamad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Uthman, from Zadhan, from 'Ali, who said: Khadijah asked the Prophet ﷺ about two sons who had died for her in the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance). The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "They are in the Fire." When he saw the aversion in her face, he said: "If you saw their place, you would hate them." She said: "O Messenger of Allah, and my child from you?" He said: "In Paradise." He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed the believers and their children are in Paradise, and indeed the polytheists and their children are in the Fire." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: ﴿And those who believed and whose offspring followed them in faith, We join with them their offspring﴾ [the verse] [[Addition from M.]] [[Zawa'id of 'Abd Allah on the Musnad (1/134). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/217): "In it is Muhammad ibn 'Uthman, whom I do not know, and the rest of its narrators are narrators of the Sahih."]].

This is His grace toward the children through the blessing of the fathers' deeds. As for His grace toward the fathers through the blessing of the children's supplication, Imam Ahmad said:

Yazid narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed Allah raises the degree of the righteous servant in Paradise, so he says: 'O Lord, how is this for me?' He says: 'By the seeking of forgiveness for you by your child.'" [[Musnad (2/509).]].

Its chain is sahih (authentic), and they did not transmit it by this route. But it has a witness in Sahih Muslim, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "When the son of Adam dies, his deeds are cut off except for three: ongoing charity, or knowledge from which benefit is gained, or a righteous child who supplicates for him." [[Sahih Muslim no. (1631).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿Every person is a pledge for what he has earned﴾. When He informed of the station of grace, which is the raising of the offspring's degree to the rank of the fathers without a deed that would necessitate it, He informed of the station of justice, which is that He does not hold anyone to account for the sin of another. Rather, ﴿every person is a pledge for what he has earned﴾, meaning: held in pledge by his deed. The sin of others among people is not laid upon him, whether that other is a father or a son, as He said: ﴿Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned, except the companions of the right, in gardens, asking one another about the guilty﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 38-41].

* *

His saying: ﴿And We provided them with fruit and meat of whatever they desire﴾, meaning: And We extended to them fruits and meats of various kinds, of what is delicious and desired.

* *

His saying: ﴿They pass therein a cup, wherein is no idle talk nor sinfulness﴾, meaning: they pass among themselves a cup, that is, of wine. This was said by al-Dahhak. ﴿Wherein is no idle talk nor sinfulness﴾, meaning: they do not speak with vain speech about it, that is, nonsense, nor sin, that is, obscenity, as the drinkers of the people of this world speak.

Ibn 'Abbas said: Al-laghw is falsehood, and al-ta'thim is lying.

Mujahid said: They do not revile one another, nor are they made to sin.

Qatadah said: That was in this world, with the devil.

So Allah has purified the wine of the Hereafter from the filth and harm of the wine of this world. He negated from it, as has preceded, the headache, the stomach-ache, and the complete removal of the intellect. He informed that it does not move them to bad, empty speech free of benefit, which contains nonsense and obscenity. He informed of its fine appearance and the goodness of its taste and its effect, saying: ﴿White, delicious to the drinkers, no ghawl in it, nor are they affected by it (yunzafun)﴾ [al-Saffat: 46-47]. He said: ﴿They are not affected by headache therefrom, nor are they intoxicated﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 19]. And here He said: ﴿They pass therein a cup, wherein is no idle talk nor sinfulness﴾.

* *

His saying: ﴿And there will circulate among them young boys (ghilman) belonging to them, as if they were pearls well-guarded﴾: an informing about their servants and attendants in Paradise, as if they were fresh pearls, hidden in their beauty, radiance, [[In M: "and their whiteness".]] cleanliness, and goodness of attire, as He said: ﴿There will circulate among them immortal youths with cups, and ewers, and a cup from a flowing spring﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 17-18].

* *

His saying: ﴿And they will turn to one another, questioning﴾, meaning: they turn to conversing and asking one another about their deeds and conditions in the worldly life. This is like the way people of drinking converse over their drinks when drink has taken hold of them, about what their affairs were.

﴿They said: Indeed we were, before, among our families, fearful﴾, meaning: we were in the worldly abode, and we were among our families, fearful of our Lord, anxious of His punishment and retribution. ﴿So Allah bestowed favor upon us and protected us from the punishment of the scorching wind﴾, meaning: He showed kindness to us and granted us refuge from what we feared.

﴿Indeed we used to call upon Him before﴾, meaning: we used to humble ourselves before Him, so Allah responded to us [Allah] [[Addition from A.]] and gave us our request. ﴿Indeed He is the Good, the Merciful﴾.

A hadith has been transmitted in this context, which al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar related in his Musnad, saying: Salamah ibn Shabib narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Dinar narrated to us, al-Rabi' ibn Subayh narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, they long for their brothers. So the couch of one comes until it faces the couch of the other, and they converse. This one reclines and that one reclines, and they converse about what was in the world. One of them says to his companion: 'O so-and-so, do you know which day Allah forgave us? The day we were in such-and-such a place, and we called upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and He forgave us.'"

Then al-Bazzar said: We do not know it to be narrated except by this chain [[Musnad al-Bazzar no. (3553), Kashf al-Astar. This is like the way people of drinking converse over their drinks when drink has taken hold of them, about what their affairs were.

﴿They said: Indeed we were, before, among our families, fearful﴾, meaning: we were in the worldly abode, and we were among our families, fearful of our Lord, anxious of His punishment and retribution. ﴿So Allah bestowed favor upon us and protected us from the punishment of the scorching wind﴾, meaning: He showed kindness to us and granted us refuge from what we feared.

﴿Indeed we used to call upon Him before﴾, meaning: we used to humble ourselves before Him, so Allah responded to us [Allah] [[Addition from A.]] and gave us our request. ﴿Indeed He is the Good, the Merciful﴾.

A hadith has been transmitted in this context, which al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar related in his Musnad, saying: Salamah ibn Shabib narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Dinar narrated to us, al-Rabi' ibn Subayh narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, they long for their brothers. So the couch of one comes until it faces the couch of the other, and they converse. This one reclines and that one reclines, and they converse about what was in the world. One of them says to his companion: 'O so-and-so, do you know which day Allah forgave us? The day we were in such-and-such a place, and we called upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and He forgave us.'"

Then al-Bazzar said: We do not know it to be narrated except by this chain [[Musnad al-Bazzar no. (3553), Kashf al-Astar. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/421): "Its narrators are narrators of the Sahih except Sa'id ibn Dinar and al-Rabi' ibn Subayh, who are weak, though both have been declared trustworthy."]].

I say: Sa'id ibn Dinar al-Dimashqi - Abu Hatim said: he is unknown (majhul). His teacher al-Rabi' ibn Subayh has been criticized by more than one scholar in respect of his memory, but he is a righteous man, trustworthy in himself.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Amr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Awdi narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from 'A'ishah: that she recited this verse: ﴿So Allah bestowed favor upon us and protected us from the punishment of the scorching wind. Indeed we used to call upon Him before. Indeed He is the Good, the Merciful﴾, and she said: "O Allah, bestow favor upon us and protect us from the punishment of the scorching wind; indeed You are the Good, the Merciful." It was said to al-A'mash: In the prayer? He said: Yes [[Related by 'Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman, as in al-Durr al-Manthur of al-Suyuti (7/634).]].

Allah says, commanding His Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, to convey His message to His servants and to remind them of what Allah has revealed to him. Then He negated from him what the people of slander and wickedness accuse him of, saying: ﴿So remind, for by the grace of your Lord you are neither a soothsayer nor a madman.﴾ That is: by the grace of Allah you are not a soothsayer, as the ignorant among the disbelievers of Quraysh claim. Then Allah said, rebuking them for their saying about the Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him: ﴿Or do they say, "A poet, for whom we await the misfortunes of time"?﴾ That is: the calamities of time. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Were they created from nothing, or are they the creators?﴾ That is: were they brought into existence without any originator? Or did they bring themselves into existence? That is: neither of these is the case. Rather, Allah is the One who created them and brought them into being after they were nothing worth mentioning.

Al-Bukhari said: Al-Humaydi narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, who said: "They narrated to me from al-Zuhri, from Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im, from his father, who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) reciting in the Maghrib prayer with al-Tur. When he reached this verse: ﴿Were they created from nothing, or are they the creators? Or did they create the heavens and the earth? Rather, they do not have certainty. Or do they have the treasuries of your Lord, or are they the controllers?﴾, my heart nearly flew away." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4854).]]

This hadith is recorded in the Two Sahihs (Bukhari and Muslim) through several chains from al-Zuhri, with the same wording. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (765), (4023), and Sahih Muslim, no. (463).]] Jubayr ibn Mut'im came to the Prophet (ﷺ) after the Battle of Badr to negotiate the ransom of the captives, and at that time he was a polytheist. His hearing of this verse from this surah was among the things that moved him to enter Islam afterward.

Then Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Or did they create the heavens and the earth? Rather, they do not have certainty.﴾ That is: did they create the heavens and the earth? This is a rebuke against them for their polytheism toward Allah, while they know that He alone is the Creator, with no partner. But their lack of certainty is what drives them to this. ﴿Or do they have the treasuries of your Lord, or are they the controllers?﴾ That is: do they have the authority to dispose of the kingdom, with the keys of the treasuries in their hands? ﴿Or are they the controllers?﴾ That is: are they the ones who call creation to account? The matter is not so; rather, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is the Owner, the Disposer, the One who does whatever He wills.

* *

His saying: ﴿Or do they have a ladder by which they listen?﴾ That is: a stairway to the Highest Assembly. ﴿Then let their listener bring a clear authority.﴾ That is: let the one who listens for them bring a manifest proof for the validity of what they do and say. That is, they have no way to that, so they have nothing and no evidence.

Then He said, rebuking them for what they attributed to Him of daughters, and for their making the angels females, and their choosing males for themselves over females, to the extent that when one of them is given the good news of a female, his face remains darkened while he is inwardly distressed. [[Ibn Kathir's text continues from the verse ﴿Do they attribute daughters to Him while you have sons?﴾ in the surah.]] Yet they have made the angels daughters of Allah and worshipped them alongside Allah. So He said: ﴿For Him are daughters, and for you are sons?﴾ This is a severe threat and a firm warning. ﴿Or do you ask them for a reward?﴾ That is: a wage for your conveying to them the message of Allah? That is: you do not ask them for anything in return. ﴿So they are burdened with debt?﴾ That is: they are weighed down and oppressed by anything they find burdensome and hard to bear. ﴿Or do they have the unseen, so that they write it down?﴾ That is: the matter is not so, for none among the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth knows the unseen except Allah. ﴿Or do they intend a plot? Then those who disbelieve, they are the ones plotted against.﴾ Allah, the Exalted, says: do these people, by their saying this about the Messenger and the religion, intend to deceive people and to plot against the Messenger and his companions? Their plot will return its evil upon themselves. So those who disbelieve are the ones who will be plotted against. ﴿Or do they have a god other than Allah? Glory be to Allah above what they associate.﴾ This is a severe rebuke of the polytheists for their worship of idols and rivals alongside Allah. Then He declared His noble self free of what they say, invent, and associate, saying: ﴿Glory be to Allah above what they associate.﴾

His saying: ﴿And be patient for the decision of your Lord, for indeed you are under Our eyes﴾ means: be patient over their harm and do not care about them, for you are in Our sight and under Our protection, and Allah will protect you from the people.

* *

His saying: ﴿And exalt your Lord with praise when you arise﴾ — al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: that is, to the prayer: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You, blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god but You."

The same has been narrated from Rabīʿ ibn Anas, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and others.

Muslim related in his Sahih from ʿUmar that he would say this at the beginning of the prayer. Aḥmad and the authors of the Sunan related it from Abu Saʿid and others, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he would say it.

Abu al-Jawzaʾ said: ﴿And exalt your Lord with praise when you arise﴾ means: when you rise from your sleep, from your bed. Ibn Jarir preferred this view, and it is supported by what Imam Aḥmad related:

Al-Walīd ibn Muslim narrated to us, al-Awzāʿī narrated to us, ʿUmayr ibn Hāniʾ narrated to me, Junādah ibn Abi Umayyah narrated to me, ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who said: "Whoever wakes up at night and says: 'There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. To Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs the praise, and He is capable of all things. Glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, Allah is greatest, and there is no power and no might except with Allah,' then says: 'My Lord, forgive me' — or said: 'then he supplicates' — he will be answered; and if he rises and performs ablution, then prays, his prayer will be accepted."

Al-Bukhari in his Sahih, and the authors of the Sunan, also related it from the hadith of al-Walīd ibn Muslim with the same chain.

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid: ﴿And exalt your Lord with praise when you arise﴾ — he said: "from every gathering."

Al-Thawri said, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas: ﴿And exalt your Lord with praise when you arise﴾ — he said: "When a man wishes to rise from his gathering, he says: 'Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You.'"

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu al-Nadr Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Dimashqi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Shuʿayb narrated to us, Talhah ibn ʿAmr al-Ḥaḍrami informed me, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abi Rabah, that he narrated to him concerning the saying of Allah: ﴿And exalt your Lord with praise when you arise﴾, he said: "When you rise from every gathering. If you have done good, you have increased in good; and if it was otherwise, this will be an expiation for it."

ʿAbd al-Razzaq said in his Jamiʿ: Maʿmar informed us, from ʿAbd al-Karim al-Jazari, from Abu ʿUthman al-Faqir, that Jibril taught the Prophet (ﷺ), when he rose from a gathering, to say: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You. I bear witness that there is no god but You. I seek Your forgiveness and turn to You in repentance." Maʿmar said: I heard others say: "This statement is the expiation of gatherings."

This is a mursal report. There are, however, connected hadiths from various routes that strengthen one another regarding this. Among them is the hadith of Ibn Jurayj, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever sits in a gathering where much idle talk occurs, and before he rises from his gathering says: 'Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You. I bear witness that there is no god but You. I seek Your forgiveness and turn to You in repentance,' he will be forgiven for whatever was said in that gathering."

Al-Tirmidhi related it, and this is his wording, and al-Nasa'i in ʿAmal al-Yawm wa al-Layla, from the hadith of Ibn Jurayj. Al-Tirmidhi said: hasan sahih. Al-Hakim related it in his Mustadrak and said: its isnad is according to the condition of Muslim, except that al-Bukhari gave it a defect.

I say: Imam Aḥmad, al-Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Hatim, Abu Zurʿah, al-Daraqutni and others gave it a defect, and attributed the error in it to Ibn Jurayj. However, Abu Dawud related it in his Sunan from a route other than Ibn Jurayj, to Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), similarly. Abu Dawud related it, and the wording is his, as did al-Nasa'i and al-Hakim in the Mustadrak, through the route of al-Hajjaj ibn Dinar, from Hashim, from Abu al-ʿAliyah, from Abu Barzah al-Aslami who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say at the end, when he wished to rise from the gathering: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You. I bear witness that there is no god but You. I seek Your forgiveness and turn to You in repentance." A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, you are saying a statement you did not used to say before?" He said: "It is an expiation for what occurs in the gathering."

It has also been narrated as mursal from Abu al-ʿAliyah, and Allah knows best. Al-Nasa'i and al-Hakim related it in the same way from the hadith of al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas, from Abu al-ʿAliyah, from Rafiʿ ibn Khadij, from the Prophet (ﷺ), the same in meaning. It was also narrated as mursal, and Allah knows best. Abu Dawud similarly related from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr that he said: "Words which no one speaks in his gathering when he rises, three times, except that they are an expiation for it, and he does not say them in a gathering of good or a gathering of remembrance except that he is sealed with them, just as a seal is stamped upon a page: 'Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You. There is no god but You. I seek Your forgiveness and turn to You in repentance.'" Al-Hakim related it from the hadith of Umm al-Mu'minin ʿAʾishah and authenticated it, and from the narration of Jubayr ibn Mut'im. Abu Bakr al-Isma'ili related it from the Commander of the Faithful ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab. All of them are from the Prophet (ﷺ). I have devoted a separate treatise to this, mentioning its routes, wordings, defects, and related matters, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace. [Note: I mentioned the hadiths on the expiation of the gathering at the explanation of Surat al-Saffat in its conclusion.]

* *

His saying: ﴿And during the night, glorify Him﴾ means: remember Him and worship Him by recitation and prayer at night, as He said: ﴿And during part of the night, pray with it as an additional [prayer] for you; perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station.﴾ [Al-Isra': 79].

* *

His saying: ﴿And after the stars recede﴾ — it has already been mentioned in the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbas that they are the two rak'ahs before the Fajr prayer, for they are legislated at the receding of the stars, that is, at their inclining toward setting. And it has been related in a hadith of Ibn Saylan, from Abu Hurayrah, raised to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Do not leave them, even if horses drive you away," meaning the two rak'ahs of Fajr. Abu Dawud related it in his Sunan. From this hadith it is reported that some companions of Imam Aḥmad held the view that they are obligatory, but this is weak, due to the hadith: "Five prayers in the day and night." He said: "Is there anything else obligatory upon me?" He said: "No, unless you do voluntarily." [Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 46, and Muslim in his Sahih, no. 11, from the hadith of Talhah ibn ʿUbayd Allah, may Allah be pleased with him.] And it is established in the two Sahihs from ʿAʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) never showed more diligence in any supererogatory prayer than in the two rak'ahs of Fajr. In a wording of Muslim: "The two rak'ahs of Fajr are better than the world and what is in it."

End of the commentary on Surat al-Tur [and Allah knows best].
